bindings.label: A 56-year-old man has a 3-month history of asymptomatic brown follicular hyperkeratotic plaques/papules spread across the body and significant hair loss on the scalp.
56-year-old Japanese man; 3-month history of asymptomatic brown follicular hyperkeratotic plaque/papules spread across the body; significant hair loss on the scalp.
Some papules exhibited a comedo-like appearance and/or signs of infection; slight reduction in pubic and axillary hair growth.
Patient had been on dialysis for 3 years due to chronic renal failure.
No family history of similar conditions; no use of medications related to the symptoms; no exposure to dioxins; did not have COVID-19 and had not received any COVID-19 vaccines.
Blood and imaging tests showed normal blood dioxin and sex hormone levels, and no signs of malignancies or collagen diseases.
Skin biopsy shows dilated infundibula, keratin plugs, lichenoid reaction, and perifollicular fibrosis.
Skin biopsy shows follicular plugging, lichenoid infiltrate, and vacuolar alteration.
No explicit transepidermal elimination is identified on histology.
